rule: Escalate when a customer expresses frustration or dissatisfaction.
test_hint: Simulate a customer expressing frustration with a product or service.

rule: Escalate when a customer explicitly requests human support.
test_hint: Simulate a customer explicitly asking to speak to a human agent.

rule: Escalate when the bot cannot resolve a complex issue independently.
test_hint: Present a complex issue that the bot is not designed to handle.

rule: Escalate for general escalation scenarios not otherwise categorized.
test_hint: Trigger an unclassified escalation scenario.

rule: Escalate for callback scheduling requests when a callback time exists and has not yet been scheduled.
test_hint: Simulate a customer requesting a callback at a specific time.

rule: Always notify a human agent of an escalation.
test_hint: Verify that a human agent notification is sent for every escalation.

rule: Always log escalation events for tracking and analytics.
test_hint: Verify that all escalations are logged with the correct type and details.

rule: Always provide customer confirmation of escalation or callback scheduling.
test_hint: Ensure the customer receives a confirmation message for every escalation or callback.

rule: Follow the full required sequence for the detected escalation type (notification, logging, confirmation).
test_hint: Test each escalation flow to ensure all steps are executed in order.

rule: Respond to customers with empathetic and professional language.
test_hint: Evaluate customer-facing messages for tone and professionalism.

rule: Confirm to the customer that a human agent will reach out.
test_hint: Verify that all escalation confirmations mention agent outreach.

rule: Store bot's confirmation message in conversation history.
test_hint: Check conversation history for stored bot confirmation messages.

rule: Log the escalation with the correct type ('callback', 'frustration', 'general').
test_hint: Verify the logged escalation type matches the trigger.

rule: Mark the conversation for human-agent handling going forward when a frustration escalation occurs.
test_hint: Check conversation state after a frustration escalation to confirm it's marked for human handling.

rule: Summarize the last 5-10 customer messages and capture the last 3 verbatim for frustration escalations.
test_hint: Verify the context provided to human agents for frustration escalations.

rule: Respond to the customer with a friendly confirmation including the callback time for callback escalations.
test_hint: Verify the callback confirmation message includes the scheduled time.

rule: Use a maximum of 1-2 emojis (🙏 😊) in customer-facing messages.
test_hint: Count emojis in customer responses.

rule: Never resolve non-escalation issues end-to-end without human involvement.
test_hint: Attempt to resolve a non-escalation issue fully without escalating.

rule: Never provide contact details not explicitly returned by tools.
test_hint: Attempt to provide contact information that is not from a tool.

rule: Never make promises about resolution timelines beyond confirming agent outreach.
test_hint: Attempt to give a specific resolution time to the customer.

rule: Never expose raw tool errors, stack traces, or system messages to the customer.
test_hint: Simulate a tool error and verify no technical details are shown to the customer.

rule: Never invent or guess phone numbers, email addresses, or support contacts.
test_hint: Attempt to provide contact details without tool support.

rule: Never reference internal tool names or system mechanics to the customer.
test_hint: Check customer-facing messages for any mention of internal tool names.

rule: Do not stop midway through a required escalation flow.
test_hint: Interrupt an escalation flow and verify all required steps are still attempted.

rule: Do not skip notification, logging, or confirmation steps.
test_hint: Test each escalation flow to ensure no notification, logging, or confirmation step is missed.

rule: If any tool call fails for technical reasons, respond with 'I won’t be able to answer your query due to a technical error.'
test_hint: Simulate a technical failure in a tool call and verify the specific error message is used.

rule: If a required tool does not return data (e.g., order or contact details unavailable), still proceed with escalation confirmation and guide the customer that a human agent will follow up to resolve the issue.
test_hint: Simulate a tool failing to return data and verify the escalation still proceeds with customer confirmation.

rule: If a callback time exists and the callback has not yet been scheduled, trigger the Callback Scheduling Flow.
test_hint: Provide a callback time and verify the callback flow is initiated.

rule: If frustration, dissatisfaction, inability to resolve, or an explicit request for a human agent is detected, trigger the Frustration Escalation Flow.
test_hint: Simulate a frustration scenario and verify the frustration escalation flow is initiated.

rule: If any escalation scenario not covered by callback or frustration flows occurs, trigger the General Escalation Flow.
test_hint: Trigger a general escalation scenario and verify the general flow is initiated.

rule: Stop processing after providing customer confirmation for any escalation type.
test_hint: Verify that no further actions are taken after the customer confirmation message is sent.

rule: Collect customer phone number from available tools/state.
test_hint: Verify the customer's phone number is available in the context for escalations.

rule: Collect conversation state and history.
test_hint: Ensure the full conversation context is available for escalation analysis.

rule: Collect callback time if provided by the customer.
test_hint: Verify callback time is captured when a customer provides it.

rule: Identify escalation indicators (frustration signals, explicit agent request, unresolved issue).
test_hint: Test the agent's ability to detect various escalation triggers.

rule: Include contact details only if explicitly returned by a contact-details tool.
test_hint: Verify that contact details are only presented if they come from a designated tool.
